title: Information gain
summary: What should you check next? State a yes-or-no belief as a phrase such as “likely” (with Sherman Kent's reference range and a survey of how people read it) or as a percentage, list the checks you could make with their time cost and how likely a result is if the belief is true or false, and see each check's possible results, where each would leave your belief, and its expected information gain in bits, exact and equal to the mutual information. Separate rankings for most informative and fastest per minute, a time budget, a best next check under an objective you choose, and observed results that update your belief, show the belief change as KL divergence apart from surprise, and recompute every remaining check along a learning trail. An entropy curve, teaching presets and six offline examples. Copy the analysis or save a narrated beamdswitch deck. Works offline, from file:// and in an iframe.
